reads.note: DECISIVE READ. D is an invisible accumulator (g337/g669/g679) with no rendered counterpart at any resolution. Partial derivation is possible and is an upper bound only: the increment is +1/s plus one per masked second, both of which the controller can count on its own clock, but the reset requires the hall light to be on WHILE FOXY IS IN THE HALL, and Foxy's presence is itself no-known-observable. So a tracking controller knows D <= tracked, never D. At the 10/20 cap the largest always-safe D is 3, which leaves an upper-bound tracker almost no room

the controller has its own monotonic clock; amHour is the only in-game re-anchor and fires once per 70 s. This is the crux of the whole route problem, not a detail: the phone holds a clock to ~302 ms + drift against a 33 ms early / 99 ms late whole-schedule tolerance (n2-minustoys-0117), and the 2 Hz winding tick is the densest known re-anchor

reads.candidateSensor: a hall-region apparition classifier with a Golden Freddy class, on the lit-hall frame the Foxy check already captures; the pixels are free, the flash is not
reads.note: he IS rendered in the hall once the light is on, so a classifier is definable: g781 re-rolls his presence every second WHILE THE LIGHT IS OFF and holding the light FREEZES whatever is there (the dump's own words for why he seems to stay while you look); g865 zeroes his exposure when he is absent. Corrected 2026-09-02 (Pedro): the previous `no-known-observable` conflated read COST with invisibility. Correction to the correction, same day: the cost is NOT marginal. g779 adds +1/frame exposure WHILE THE LIGHT IS ON HIM (the summary table's 'lit empty hall' wording is looser than g779) and g780 kills above 100. A HALL_FLASH holds the light 8 frames, so flashing with him present is 8 toward a 101-frame kill -- the classification is free in pixels because the frame is already captured, but the FLASH is not free, and that is the real cost.
the AM digit is exactly this field; its read is refused mid-animation and during a blackout
